role.altitude: The research assistant keeps agreeing variables with researchers, checking model assumptions and editing text; hand-built entry forms, retyped tables, reformatted references and descriptive runs shrink.
skills_to_grow: Writing reusable analysis and table scripts and testing generated code on data with known answers
role.ambitious_version: An assistant whose tables, graphs and fact sheets rebuild themselves when the data are updated.

tasks.short: Agree variables and checks with the researcher, design and create special programs for data entry and cleaning and for statistical analysis, test them and document them.

steps.what: Research assistant agrees the variables, codes and checks with the researcher
Research assistant creates data entry programs with validation checks
Research assistant writes cleaning and statistical analysis programs

loop.input: The variable list, codebook and a description of each cleaning or analysis step; no respondent data.
loop.check: Each script runs on a test file with known answers before use on real data; the assistant reads every line.
loop.stop: One draft per step; the assistant edits from there.

steps.what: Research assistant tests and documents the programs

tasks.design: Data entry runs in a configured electronic data capture tool with conditional logic and range checks instead of hand-built spreadsheet forms. A coding assistant drafts cleaning and analysis scripts from the codebook, without seeing respondent data, and every script is tested on a file with known answers. Agreeing variables and testing stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Entry forms and scripts were built from scratch per study.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable data capture tools and coding assistants.
tasks.still_hard: Messy legacy data with unclear codes.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a variable means in the study.
tasks.altitude: Less building from scratch; checking stays.

reach.learn: Whether validated forms cut entry errors.

evidence.claim: A data capture tool offers forms with conditional logic and an audit trail.
Coding assistants draft scripts from a description.
Research use of personal data needs safeguards such as pseudonymisation.

assumptions: Boundary: building entry and analysis programs; running analyses is a separate task.
The data capture tool is licensed by the institute and approved for personal data.
Agreeing variables keeps its full time. Testing and documenting (s4) keep their full time: the design names nothing that removes part of them.
unknowns: Share of studies with legacy data.
research_questions: Do script errors found after use fall?

already_counted.description: Research assistant reads and tests drafted scripts.

incremental.description: Research assistant builds test files with known answers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off studies with unusual data, where the entry tool fits poorly (s2 keeps 80) and drafted scripts need heavy rework (s3 keeps 90) (8.0); high: repeated surveys with standard variables (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather inputs, format project-related reports and manuscripts, check references, prepare presentations and edit text for the researchers.

steps.what: Research assistant gathers results, figures and text from the researchers
Research assistant formats reports and manuscripts to the template or journal style
Research assistant checks references and citations
Research assistant prepares presentations from figures and key points
Research assistant edits text after the researchers' comments

tasks.design: Manuscripts are written in templates with the journal's or institute's styles, so formatting is mostly applied rather than done by hand. References are imported into a reference manager by identifier and formatted by its style file; no model writes references, and every reference not found by identifier is checked by hand. Slides come from the institute's template with figures exported at the right size.
tasks.previous_blocker: Formatting and reference styles were fixed by hand in each version.
tasks.enabler_now: Document templates with styles and reference managers with style files.
tasks.still_hard: Late changes from co-authors in different formats.
tasks.human_edge: Making a complex result clear on one slide.

reach.learn: Whether desk rejections for format fall.

evidence.claim: One model invented 55% and another 18% of the citations it generated.
Reference managers import by identifier and format by style file.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing documents for the researchers; submission is the researchers' step.
Input contract for s3: references with a DOI or ISBN, about 80%; the rest are checked by hand; s3 is priced at that share.
Editing after comments keeps its full time. Gathering inputs from researchers (s1) keeps its full time: the templates do not change how results and text are collected.
unknowns: How often co-authors bypass the template.

incremental.description: Research assistant keeps templates and style files current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off reports with unusual formats (s2 keeps 80) and many references without an identifier (s3 keeps 80) (12.5); high: frequent manuscripts to journals with standard styles (24.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare tables and graphs from analysis output, check the numbers, write fact sheets and written reports summarizing research results, have them approved and publish the approved fact sheet.

steps.what: Research assistant prepares tables and graphs from the analysis output
Research assistant checks the numbers in tables against the output
Research assistant writes fact sheets and reports summarizing research results

loop.input: The checked tables and the researcher's key messages.
loop.output: A draft fact sheet or summary in the institute's template.
loop.check: Every number in the text must match a table cell, or the draft is blocked; the assistant reads each sentence against the table it describes and the study's limits, and rewrites and edits all text.

steps.what: Lead researcher reviews and approves the final fact sheet
Research assistant checks the fact sheet before publishing: that it is the version the lead researcher approved, its figures, and the project web page it goes to
Research assistant publishes the approved fact sheet on the project website

approvals.approved_version: The fact sheet exactly as approved by the lead researcher in s4 and checked by the assistant in s4b, published once on the project website; any change goes back for approval and a new check.

tasks.design: Table and graph scripts read the analysis output files and write formatted tables and graphs, so they are rebuilt rather than retyped when the data change; the assistant spot-checks them. A bounded drafting step writes a first fact sheet from the checked tables, and a check blocks any number not found in a table. The assistant rewrites the text, the lead researcher approves, and the assistant checks that version and publishes it once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tables were copied from output into spreadsheets and documents by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Table and graph scripts over analysis output, and drafting models with number checks.
tasks.still_hard: Saying what a result means without overstating it.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the one graph a policymaker will remember.

reach.learn: Whether fact sheets arrive in time for news moments.

evidence.claim: A pharma firm reported report-writing time down 90% with people approving; vendor case.
AI-generated text published to inform the public must be disclosed unless human-edited.

assumptions: Boundary: from analysis output to published fact sheet; the analysis is a separate task.
Input contract for s1: output files written by the analysis scripts from the analysis task; about 80% of tables are standard layouts; s1 is priced at that share.
The lead researcher's time and publishing stay outside the assistant's savings or keep full time.
research_questions: Do number errors in published fact sheets fall?

already_counted.description: Research assistant rewrites drafted fact sheet text.

incremental.description: Research assistant writes table and graph scripts per project.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off reports with custom tables, so scripts cover little (s1 keeps 80) and the text is mostly written (s3 keeps 95) (16.5); high: recurring monitors with the same tables each wave (36.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the analysis dataset, perform descriptive and multivariate statistical analyses with software, check model assumptions and discuss results with the researcher.

steps.what: Research assistant prepares the analysis dataset: merging, recoding and weighting
Research assistant performs descriptive statistical analyses
Research assistant performs multivariate analyses specified by the researcher

loop.input: The researcher's model specification and the codebook; no respondent data.
loop.output: Model code for the statistics software.
loop.check: The code runs on a test file with known results; the assistant reads every line and the output.

steps.what: Research assistant checks model assumptions and discusses results with the researcher

tasks.design: The cleaning and preparation scripts from the study's programs rebuild the analysis dataset whenever data arrive, and a descriptive script writes frequencies and summaries per variable. A coding assistant drafts model code from the researcher's specification, without seeing respondent data, and the code is tested on a file with known results. Checking assumptions and interpreting stay with the assistant and researcher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each data delivery was merged, recoded and described by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Scripted pipelines in statistics software and coding assistants.
tasks.still_hard: Models whose assumptions the data break.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a result that is too good to be true.
tasks.altitude: Less routine running; statistical judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether results come back sooner after each wave.

evidence.claim: Calculations over fixed formulas are plain code; no model is needed.
Research use of personal data needs safeguards such as pseudonymisation.

assumptions: Boundary: running analyses on a prepared study; writing up is separate.
Input contract for s1: cleaned data from the data capture tool and the cleaning scripts written for the study; about 80% of deliveries follow the planned layout; s1 is priced at that share.
Checking assumptions and discussing results keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of analyses that are repeated waves.
research_questions: Are analysis errors found before reporting?

already_counted.description: Research assistant reads and tests drafted model code.

incremental.description: Research assistant maintains the descriptive script.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off studies with unusual data, so preparation (s1 keeps 85) and descriptives (s2 keeps 70) stay mostly by hand (14.5); high: repeated survey waves with the same layout (28.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
